_about: Big movements (religious, intellectual, political, social) attached to the states and years where they mattered, written for GeoHistory from general knowledge (AI-written, shown with that label). 'states' are the territory names on the maps; 'from'/'to' are the movement's conventional dates, shown as written. Every entry names its English Wikipedia article in 'wiki' and 'source'; tools/context/build_context.py checks 'from' against the article's Wikidata item (inception P571 or start time P580, 5 years of slack; 15 for movements dated by century) and writes the result to 'verified' (true, false, or null when Wikidata has no start date). 'text' is one line.

movements.name: Protestant Reformation
movements.text: Break with the Roman Church that began with Martin Luther's 95 theses (1517) and produced Lutheran, Reformed and Anglican churches.

movements.name: Counter-Reformation
movements.text: Catholic renewal and response to Protestantism, from the Council of Trent (1545-1563), with the Jesuits and the Inquisition.

movements.name: Hussite movement
movements.text: Followers of Jan Hus, burned at Constance in 1415, who fought off five crusades and won concessions from the Church.

movements.name: Italian Renaissance
movements.text: Revival of classical learning and art in the Italian city-states: Brunelleschi, Leonardo, Michelangelo, Machiavelli.

movements.name: Northern Renaissance
movements.text: Renaissance humanism and art north of the Alps: Erasmus, Dürer, van Eyck, Thomas More.

movements.name: Scientific Revolution
movements.text: From Copernicus (1543) to Newton's Principia (1687): observation, experiment and mathematics remade astronomy and physics.

movements.name: Age of Enlightenment
movements.text: Reason, science and rights against custom and absolutism: Locke, Voltaire, Montesquieu, Rousseau, Kant, Hume.

movements.name: Industrial Revolution
movements.text: Shift to machine production, steam power and factories, beginning in Britain's textile and iron industries.

movements.name: Second Industrial Revolution
movements.text: Steel, electricity, chemicals, railways and the telephone: mass production in Germany and the United States.

movements.name: Abolitionism in the United Kingdom
movements.text: Campaign against the slave trade (abolished 1807) and slavery in the colonies (Slavery Abolition Act 1833): Clarkson, Wilberforce, Equiano.

movements.name: Abolitionism in the United States
movements.text: Movement to end slavery, from Garrison's Liberator (1831) and Frederick Douglass to the Thirteenth Amendment (1865).

movements.name: Abolitionism in Brazil
movements.text: Campaign that ended the slave trade (1850) and slavery itself with the Golden Law of 1888, the last in the Americas.

movements.name: Romanticism
movements.text: Art and thought of feeling, nature and the nation, against Enlightenment rationalism: Goethe, Wordsworth, Byron, Beethoven.

movements.name: French Revolution and Jacobinism
movements.text: Radical republicanism of the Jacobin Club, which led the Revolution's most radical phase and the Terror (1793-1794).

movements.name: Revolutions of 1848
movements.text: Liberal and national revolutions across Europe: the 'Springtime of Nations', mostly crushed within two years.

movements.name: Risorgimento
movements.text: Movement for Italian unity and independence: Mazzini, Garibaldi and Cavour; the Kingdom of Italy was proclaimed in 1861.

movements.name: German nationalism and unification
movements.text: Drive for a German nation-state, from the student fraternities of 1815 to Bismarck's empire of 1871.

movements.name: Pan-Slavism
movements.text: Idea of the unity of the Slavic peoples, used by Russia to back the Balkan Slavs against the Ottomans and Austria.

movements.name: Marxism and the socialist movement
movements.text: Workers' parties and trade unions inspired by Marx and Engels (Communist Manifesto, 1848): the SPD, the Second International.

movements.name: Bolsheviks
movements.text: Lenin's faction of the Russian Social Democratic Labour Party (split of 1903), which seized power in October 1917.

movements.name: Communism (Marxism-Leninism)
movements.text: State ideology of the Soviet Union and the states modelled on it: one party, planned economy, rule in the name of the working class.

movements.name: Italian Fascism
movements.text: Mussolini's movement: nationalist, anti-communist, violent, ruling Italy as a one-party dictatorship from 1922-1925 to 1943.

movements.name: Nazism
movements.text: Hitler's racist, antisemitic and totalitarian ideology; the Nazi Party ruled Germany 1933-1945 and carried out the Holocaust.

movements.name: Francoism
movements.text: Franco's authoritarian, Catholic-nationalist regime after the Civil War, with the Falange as the single party.

movements.name: Estado Novo (Portugal)
movements.text: Salazar's corporatist dictatorship, ended by the Carnation Revolution of 1974.

movements.name: Women's suffrage in the United Kingdom
movements.wiki: Women's suffrage in the United Kingdom
movements.text: Campaign for women's votes, by suffragists and the militant suffragettes of the WSPU (1903); partial suffrage 1918, equal 1928.

movements.name: Women's suffrage in the United States
movements.wiki: Women's suffrage in the United States
movements.text: From the Seneca Falls Convention (1848) to the Nineteenth Amendment (1920).

movements.name: Progressive Era
movements.text: Reform against corruption, monopolies and child labour; trust-busting, food safety laws, direct election of senators.

movements.name: Temperance movement and Prohibition
movements.text: Nationwide ban on alcohol under the Eighteenth Amendment, repealed in 1933.

movements.name: Civil rights movement
movements.text: Struggle against segregation and for Black voting rights: Brown v. Board (1954), Montgomery, King, Civil Rights Act 1964, Voting Rights Act 1965.

movements.name: Anti-apartheid movement
movements.text: Resistance to racial segregation laws by the ANC and others: Defiance Campaign, Sharpeville (1960), Soweto (1976), Mandela.

movements.name: Indian independence movement
movements.text: From the Indian National Congress (1885) to Gandhi's non-violent campaigns (Salt March 1930, Quit India 1942) and independence in 1947.

movements.name: Decolonisation of the British Empire
movements.text: End of the European colonial empires after the Second World War: India 1947, Indonesia 1949, most of Africa 1957-1975.

movements.name: Decolonisation of Africa
movements.text: Independence of African colonies, from Libya (1951) and Ghana (1957) to Zimbabwe (1980).

movements.name: Pan-Africanism
movements.text: Solidarity of Africans and the African diaspora: the Pan-African Congresses, Nkrumah, the Organisation of African Unity (1963).

movements.name: Arab nationalism
movements.text: From the Arab Revolt of 1916 to Nasser's pan-Arabism and the Ba'ath parties.

movements.name: Zionism
movements.text: Movement for a Jewish homeland in Palestine, organised by Herzl's First Zionist Congress (1897); Israel was founded in 1948.

movements.name: Young Turks
movements.text: Constitutionalist reformers whose revolution of 1908 restored the constitution; their CUP ruled the empire through the First World War.

movements.name: Tanzimat
movements.text: Ottoman reforms of law, army, schools and taxation, with equality of Muslims and non-Muslims before the law.

movements.name: Kemalism
movements.text: Atatürk's reforms: a secular republic, Latin alphabet, Western law and dress, under the Republican People's Party.

movements.name: Self-Strengthening Movement
movements.text: Qing reforms after the Opium Wars: arsenals, shipyards and Western technology under Confucian rule.

movements.name: Taiping Heavenly Kingdom
movements.text: Millenarian Christian-inspired rebellion of Hong Xiuquan; one of the deadliest wars in history.

movements.name: May Fourth Movement
movements.text: Student-led nationalist and cultural movement after the Treaty of Versailles gave Shandong to Japan; seedbed of the Chinese Communist Party.

movements.name: Cultural Revolution
movements.text: Mao's campaign against 'bourgeois' elements: Red Guards, purges, persecution and mass deaths.

movements.name: Meiji Restoration and modernisation
movements.text: Restoration of imperial rule and rapid Westernising reform: an army, railways, schools and the constitution of 1889.

movements.name: Freedom and People's Rights Movement
movements.text: Campaign for an elected assembly and a constitution in Meiji Japan.

movements.name: Solidarity
movements.text: Independent trade union led by Lech Wałęsa, banned under martial law (1981), which won the semi-free election of 1989.

movements.name: Prague Spring
movements.text: Dubček's 'socialism with a human face', ended by the Warsaw Pact invasion of August 1968.

movements.name: Chartism
movements.text: Working-class movement for the People's Charter: votes for all men, secret ballot, paid MPs.

movements.name: Irish nationalism and Home Rule
movements.text: From Parnell's Home Rule campaign to the Easter Rising (1916), the War of Independence and the Irish Free State (1922).

movements.name: Spanish American wars of independence
movements.text: Creole-led wars that ended Spanish rule on the mainland of the Americas: Bolívar, San Martín, Hidalgo.

movements.name: American Revolution
movements.text: Colonial resistance to British taxation that became a war of independence (1775-1783) and a federal republic under the Constitution of 1787.

movements.name: Great Awakenings
movements.text: Protestant revival of camp meetings and new churches that fed the temperance and abolition movements.

movements.name: Labor movement in the United States
movements.wiki: Labor movement in the United States
movements.text: Unions from the Knights of Labor and the AFL to the strikes of the 1930s and the Wagner Act (1935).

movements.name: New Deal
movements.text: Roosevelt's programmes against the Great Depression: relief, public works, Social Security, bank and labour reform.

movements.name: McCarthyism
movements.text: The Second Red Scare: loyalty oaths, blacklists and Senator McCarthy's accusations of communist subversion.

movements.name: Counterculture of the 1960s and anti-war movement
movements.wiki: Opposition to United States involvement in the Vietnam War
movements.text: Mass protest against the Vietnam War, campus revolts and the youth counterculture.

movements.name: Second-wave feminism
movements.text: Campaigns for equal pay, reproductive rights and against discrimination in law and work.

movements.name: May 68
movements.text: Student revolt and general strike that shook de Gaulle's France in May and June 1968.

movements.name: European integration
movements.text: From the Coal and Steel Community (1951) and the Treaty of Rome (1957) to the European Union (1993) and the euro.

movements.name: Perestroika and glasnost
movements.text: Gorbachev's restructuring of the economy and openness in public life, which ended in the Soviet Union's dissolution.

movements.name: Revolutions of 1989
movements.text: Fall of the communist governments of Central and Eastern Europe; the Berlin Wall opened on 9 November 1989.

movements.name: Iranian Revolution and Islamism
movements.text: Revolution that overthrew the Shah and made Iran an Islamic republic under Ayatollah Khomeini.

movements.name: Arab Spring
movements.text: Wave of protests and uprisings from Tunisia (December 2010) that toppled rulers in Tunisia, Egypt, Libya and Yemen.

movements.name: Wahhabism
movements.text: Strict Sunni revival of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, allied with the House of Saud since 1744.

movements.name: Khalsa and the rise of the Sikhs
movements.text: Order of initiated Sikhs founded by Guru Gobind Singh (1699), the core of later Sikh power in the Punjab.

movements.name: Bhakti movement
movements.text: Devotional Hinduism in the vernacular languages: Kabir, Mirabai, Tulsidas, Chaitanya.

movements.name: Neo-Confucianism
movements.text: Revival of Confucian philosophy by Zhu Xi and others; the basis of the civil-service examinations until 1905.

movements.name: Crusading movement
movements.text: Papal call to armed pilgrimage to take and hold Jerusalem, from Urban II (1095) to the fall of Acre (1291).

movements.name: Reconquista
movements.text: Christian kingdoms' reconquest of Iberia from Muslim rule, ending with the fall of Granada in 1492.

movements.name: Cluniac and Gregorian reforms
movements.text: Church reform against simony and lay control, which led to the Investiture Controversy with the emperors.

movements.name: Scholasticism and the first universities
movements.text: Method of reasoned inquiry taught at Bologna, Paris and Oxford: Abelard, Aquinas, Ockham.

movements.name: Islamic Golden Age
movements.text: Flowering of science, medicine and philosophy: the House of Wisdom, al-Khwarizmi, Ibn Sina, Ibn Rushd.

movements.name: Safavid Shi'ism
movements.wiki: Safavid conversion of Iran to Shia Islam
movements.text: Ismail I made Twelver Shia Islam the state religion in 1501 and the Safavids converted most of Iran.

movements.name: Hellenism
movements.text: Spread of Greek language, cities and learning across the lands Alexander conquered; Alexandria's Library and Museum.

movements.name: Spread of Christianity
movements.text: From a persecuted Jewish sect to the empire's favoured faith under Constantine (313) and its state religion (380).

movements.name: Ashoka's Buddhism
movements.text: After the Kalinga war Ashoka promoted Buddhist ethics (dhamma) in edicts across his empire and sent missions abroad.

movements.name: Hundred Schools of Thought
movements.text: Confucians, Mohists, Daoists and Legalists debated how to govern in the Warring States era.

movements.name: Athenian democracy
movements.text: Rule by the assembly of male citizens, from Cleisthenes' reforms (508 BC) to the Macedonian conquest.

movements.name: Mfecane
movements.text: Wars and migrations in southern Africa around the rise of the Zulu kingdom under Shaka.

movements.name: Fulani jihads
movements.text: Islamic reform wars across West Africa that founded the Sokoto Caliphate (1804) and other states.

movements.name: Balkan national revivals
movements.text: Language, schools and churches of the Balkan nations, and their risings against Ottoman rule.

movements.name: Greek War of Independence
movements.text: Uprising against Ottoman rule supported by Britain, France and Russia; Greece became independent in 1830.

movements.name: Non-cooperation and civil disobedience
movements.text: Gandhi's first mass campaign: boycott of British goods, courts and schools.

movements.name: Khmer Rouge
movements.text: Communist movement under Pol Pot that ruled 1975-1979 and killed between 1.5 and 2 million people.

movements.name: Peronism
movements.text: Juan and Eva Perón's movement of organised labour, nationalism and social welfare.

movements.name: Mexican Revolution
movements.text: Revolt against Porfirio Díaz that became a civil war of Madero, Villa, Zapata and Carranza; constitution of 1917.

movements.name: Cuban Revolution
movements.text: Castro's 26th of July Movement overthrew Batista in January 1959; Cuba became a communist state.

movements.name: Environmental movement
movements.text: From Rachel Carson's Silent Spring (1962) and Earth Day (1970) to green parties and climate campaigns.

movements.name: Gay liberation
movements.text: Movement for gay and lesbian rights after the Stonewall riots of 1969.
